Marathon Petroleum rose 1.4% today, recovering from four consecutive days of losses that had wiped out 5.6% since early November. The bounce came as oil prices steadied—U.S. crude held at $99.64 per barrel after dipping below $90 last week on hopes for an Iran peace deal—while refineries continued running at a healthy 94.5% capacity. The stock had fallen sharply when Iran conflict headlines suggested a near-term resolution might ease global oil markets, but today's modest rebound suggests the market is recalibrating expectations: peace talks remain stalled according to Secretary of State Rubio, and Trump's optimistic rhetoric about ending the conflict "fairly soon" has not yet translated into a deal.

The refiner is also benefiting from steady underlying demand conditions; gasoline and diesel inventories remain moderate (around 209 million and 99 million barrels respectively), which supports margins. That said, the stock remains down nearly 6% over two weeks as investors weigh the competing forces of geopolitical risk premium in oil prices against the possibility that a resolution could flatten the crude market in coming months.
